lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and create root endpoint
steps.instructions: Run pip install fastapi uvicorn in your terminal, then create main.py in your project directory. Import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), and define a GET / route that returns Hello World.

targets.caption: Install FastAPI and Uvicorn in the terminal
Create the app and root GET route in main.py

explanations.topic: Path decorator and root route handler

hints: Which two packages do you need to install before creating main.py?
Import FastAPI from fastapi and assign FastAPI() to app.
Decorate def root(): with @app.get("/") and return {"Hello": "World"}.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to install uvicorn alongside fastapi.
Naming the FastAPI instance something other than app when planning to run uvicorn main:app.

steps.title: Run server and verify root route
steps.instructions: Start the server with uvicorn main:app --reload. Open the printed local URL in your browser to confirm the JSON response.

targets.caption: Verify Uvicorn starts and prints the local URL
Confirm the root endpoint returns JSON in the browser

hints: Which CLI tool runs the FastAPI application?
Pass the module and app object as main:app to uvicorn.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in Chrome.
common_mistakes: Running uvicorn from outside the directory containing main.py.
Forgetting --reload so file edits do not restart the server.
Including .py in main:app (using main.py:app instead of main:app).

steps.title: Create POST endpoint to add items
steps.instructions: In main.py, add an empty items list and a POST /items endpoint that appends the item query parameter and returns the list. With uvicorn running, POST an item using curl from another terminal.

targets.caption: Server log shows the POST request

hints: Where will the to-do items be stored in memory?
Define items = [] above the routes and decorate create_item with @app.post("/items").
In create_item(item: str): call items.append(item) and return items, then test with curl -X POST.
common_mistakes: Returning item instead of items and wondering why earlier items do not appear in the response.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint for single item
steps.instructions: Add a GET /items/{item_id} endpoint taking item_id: int that returns items[item_id]. After the reload, re-add items via POST and fetch one by index with curl.

targets.caption: Define path parameter route to fetch an item
Server log shows the item fetch

explanations.topic: Path parameters and automatic int conversion
In-memory list reset on server reload

hints: How do you capture a dynamic segment in a FastAPI route path?
Put {item_id} in the route string and match the parameter name item_id: int in get_item.
Because --reload clears the in-memory items list on save, POST an item again before running curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0.
common_mistakes: Omitting the : int type hint on item_id, which leaves it as a string and causes a list indexing TypeError.
Calling GET /items/0 immediately after saving main.py without re-populating the reset items list.

steps.title: Raise 404 HTTPException for missing items
steps.instructions: Import HTTPException from fastapi and, in get_item, return the item only if item_id < len(items). Otherwise raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...) and test with curl on a missing index.

targets.caption: Return a 404 HTTPException instead of an unhandled IndexError

explanations.topic: HTTP response status codes and 404 Not Found

hints: Why does requesting a missing index currently return Internal Server Error?
Import HTTPException from fastapi and guard items[item_id] with if item_id < len(items):.
In the else branch, raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found").
common_mistakes: Returning HTTPException instead of raising it with raise.
Forgetting to import HTTPException from fastapi.

steps.title: List items with limit query parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add an @app.get("/items") endpoint list_items(limit: int = 10) that returns items[0:limit]. Add a few items, then run curl against /items with and without ?limit=3 and read the JSON list it returns.

targets.caption: Add list_items GET route with default query limit
curl returns the JSON list of items

explanations.topic: Query parameters with default values and type conversion

hints: How do you add an optional query parameter with a default value in FastAPI?
Define limit: int = 10 in def list_items(limit: int = 10): under @app.get("/items").
Slice the list with return items[0:limit] and test ?limit=3 with curl.
common_mistakes: Forgetting quotes around the URL when testing ?limit=3 in zsh/bash.
Confusing GET /items with POST /items in curl.

steps.title: Validate payloads with Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: In main.py, import BaseModel from pydantic, define class Item(BaseModel) with text: str and is_done: bool = False, and make create_item take item: Item. With uvicorn running, POST a JSON body via curl -d to /items.

targets.caption: Define the Pydantic model for JSON body validation

explanations.topic: Pydantic BaseModel for data structure and validation
JSON request payload vs query parameter
Required fields by removing default values

hints: How do you define a structured JSON request body in FastAPI?
Subclass BaseModel in class Item(BaseModel): with text: str and is_done: bool = False.
Update create_item(item: Item) and send JSON in curl using -d '{"text":"apple"}' without ?item=.
common_mistakes: Still sending ?item=apple as a query parameter after switching item: Item, which triggers a body field required error.
Leaving text: str = None when you want text to be a required field.

steps.title: Add response_model to GET endpoints
steps.instructions: In main.py, add response_model=list[Item] to the @app.get("/items") decorator and response_model=Item to @app.get("/items/{item_id}").
hints: Which keyword argument on the route decorator defines the output schema?
Add response_model=Item to @app.get("/items/{item_id}", ...).
Add response_model=list[Item] to @app.get("/items", ...).
common_mistakes: Using response_model=Item instead of response_model=list[Item] on list_items.

steps.title: Test endpoints in interactive Swagger docs
steps.instructions: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your browser, expand POST /items, click Try it out, edit the request body JSON, and click Execute.

targets.caption: Use Swagger UI at /docs to execute API requests interactively

explanations.topic: Interactive Swagger UI (/docs), ReDoc (/redoc), and openapi.json

hints: Which URL path serves FastAPI's built-in interactive Swagger UI?
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your browser.
Expand POST /items, click Try it out, fill in the text field, and click Execute.
common_mistakes: Visiting / instead of /docs when looking for Swagger UI.
Forgetting to click Execute after clicking Try it out and editing the JSON body.
